overview: Mapletree Logistics Trust (MLT) is Singapore's first Asia Pacific-focused logistics REIT, listed on the SGX Main Board in 2005. It owns and manages a diversified portfolio of 175 income-producing logistics and warehouse properties worth S$13.1 billion (as at 31 March 2026) across nine markets: Singapore, China, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Malaysia, Vietnam and India. MLT is externally managed by Mapletree Logistics Trust Management Ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mapletree Investments Pte Ltd, a Temasek-linked real estate group that also sponsors Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust and other Mapletree-branded vehicles. Fiscal year ends 31 March; results and distributions are reported in SGD.

business_model.summary: MLT earns rental income from leasing warehouse and logistics space to third-party tenants under multi-tenanted buildings (MTBs, ~79% of revenue) and single-user assets (SUAs, ~21%), then distributes substantially all distributable income to unitholders as is required of a Singapore REIT. Growth comes from (1) organic rental escalations/positive reversions and high occupancy, (2) yield-accretive acquisitions (increasingly sourced from the Mapletree sponsor's development pipeline or third parties), and (3) asset enhancement/redevelopment of existing sites to modern, higher-spec Grade A space, funded partly by selective divestment of older, lower-growth properties.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - 997 tenants, primarily 3PLs, e-commerce/consumer, F&B and electronics companies; top 10 tenants (incl. Equinix, CWT, Coles Group, HKTV, S.F. Express, Coupang, Cainiao, GXO Logistics) account for ~19.7% of gross revenue
business_model.geographic_mix: AUM by geography: Singapore 20.8%, Hong Kong SAR 22.3%, China 18.3%, Japan 13.4%, South Korea 7.5%, Australia 7.7%, Malaysia 5.9%, Vietnam 3.0%, India 1.1%. Developed markets (Singapore, Japan, Hong Kong, Australia, South Korea) make up ~70% of the portfolio by AUM and revenue, with China/emerging markets as the balance.
business_model.tenant_industry_mix: Consumer staples 15%, Others 17%, Electronics & IT 10%, F&B 14%, Fashion/Apparel/Cosmetics 6%, Materials/Construction/Engineering 6%, Automobiles 6%, Retail 5%; ~85% of revenue from tenants serving domestic consumption vs ~15% export-oriented

reit_profile.recent_divestments: Divested 6 properties in FY25/26 (Singapore x3, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia) for a combined ~S$99m, at an average ~20% premium to book valuation; S$168m divested in FY24/25. Management has identified ~S$1bn of further older-specification properties for divestment, about half located in China and Hong Kong SAR.
reit_profile.recent_acquisitions: Acquired a freehold, Grade A warehouse in Bhiwandi, Mumbai (India) for ~INR 3,888m / S$53.2m in 4Q FY25/26 (completed March 2026), 100% leased to two listed Indian food/grocery e-commerce companies with 3.9-year WALE and built-in escalations. Completed a S$205m redevelopment of Mapletree Joo Koon Logistics Hub (Singapore), now 99.3% occupied.
reit_profile.distribution_policy_change: Management discontinued the practice of distributing one-off divestment gains starting FY25/26 as a 'prudent measure' given macro uncertainty; retained divestment gains will instead be used to pay down debt or fund asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs). This mechanically lowers headline DPU versus prior years (FY23/24 and FY24/25 included S$41.6m and S$27.0m of divestment-gain distributions respectively) even though operating/same-store DPU is more stable.

main_competitors: Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust (sister Mapletree vehicle, different asset class)
Prologis (global logistics REIT with APAC exposure)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest and most geographically diversified logistics/industrial S-REITs, and the first Asia-Pacific-focused logistics REIT listed in Singapore (2005); among the largest S-REITs by AUM. Competes with regional logistics landlords and private logistics platforms (e.g., GLP, ESR, Prologis) for tenants and acquisition targets across nine Asia-Pacific markets.

moat_factors.description: Right of first refusal over logistics assets developed or warehoused by sponsor Mapletree Investments; sponsor has an active Asia-Pacific logistics development pipeline (completed projects in China, Vietnam, Australia, India totalling ~3.6m sqm GFA, plus ~1.4m sqm underway in Malaysia, Australia, India, Vietnam, Hong Kong) that can be injected into MLT once stabilised and accretive.
175 properties across nine countries and 997 tenants reduces single-market and single-tenant concentration risk; largest tenant (Equinix) is only ~3.8% of gross revenue.
Short 2.5-year WALE allows the portfolio to reprice quickly to market rents in strong markets (positive reversions ex-China), but cuts both ways in weak markets like China.

Largest solar generating capacity among reporting S-REITs (131.8 MWp) and 66-67% green-certified GFA support tenant retention (ESG-driven leasing demand) and access to green financing (S$1.5bn, ~28% of borrowings).
Fitch BBB+ stable outlook supports access to diversified, multi-currency debt markets (bonds, MTNs, loans across SGD, JPY, RMB, HKD, KRW, AUD, MYR).

weaknesses: Externally/sponsor-managed structure creates potential conflicts of interest: management fees, ROFR pricing, and acquisition/divestment decisions involve related-party transactions with the Mapletree group
Significant exposure to China (18.3% AUM / 15.1% revenue) and Hong Kong SAR (22.3% AUM / 16.9% revenue), both experiencing prolonged rental weakness and soft domestic demand
~70% of revenue derived from overseas (non-SGD) markets exposes distributable income and asset values to currency translation losses, only partially hedged
Rising aggregate leverage (40.6%, up from 36.8% three years ago) approaching regulatory/market comfort ceilings, raising refinancing-rate sensitivity
DPU has declined for multiple consecutive years on both headline and operations-adjusted basis

growth_drivers: Portfolio rejuvenation strategy: recycle capital from selective divestment of ~S$1bn of older, lower-growth assets (half in China/Hong Kong) into modern, higher-yielding Grade A logistics space
Sponsor development pipeline in India, Vietnam, Malaysia and Australia offering a visible acquisition runway (~1.4m sqm GFA underway)
Expansion into higher-growth emerging logistics markets (India, Vietnam) riding e-commerce and supply-chain diversification/'China+1' trends; India footprint now spans Pune, Delhi/Chennai and Mumbai

Structural e-commerce growth (global e-commerce sales forecast to grow from US$6.42tn in 2025 to US$7.89tn by 2028) benefiting modern logistics real estate demand, especially in markets MLT's tenant base (85% domestic consumption-oriented) serves
Supply chain resilience/diversification trends increasing demand for modern, strategically located, flexible logistics hubs

Ongoing asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs) and redevelopments (e.g., completed Joo Koon Logistics Hub in Singapore; new project planned in eastern Singapore; Subang, Malaysia redevelopment pending land amalgamation)
Continued positive rental reversions ex-China (+4.2% in 4Q FY25/26) and gradually improving China reversions (-2.0% vs -9.4% a year ago) support organic NPI growth
Proactive capital management (lower average cost of debt at 2.6%, 83% fixed-rate hedged, 75% income hedged into SGD) cushioning rate and FX volatility

business.description: China rental reversions remain negative (-2.0% to -5.7% range across periods) amid soft domestic consumption, elevated vacancy (~19.9% nationally) and new supply pressure; Hong Kong prime warehouse vacancy rose to 10.1% with weak leasing demand from 3PLs and retailers downsizing.

business.risk: Tenant/customer concentration in e-commerce and consumer sectors
business.description: Heavy reliance on consumer-facing and e-commerce tenants (Coupang, Cainiao, HKTV, S.F. Express, GXO among top 10) exposes MLT to consumer discretionary spending cycles and e-commerce logistics demand normalization.
Frequent lease renewals create reversion risk in soft markets (China) even as they offer upside in strong markets.

External manager is a Mapletree Investments subsidiary; ROFR-sourced acquisitions, management fees, and divestment counterparties can raise related-party governance concerns typical of sponsor-backed S-REITs.

financial.description: Leverage has risen from 36.8% (FY21/22) to 40.6% (FY25/26), narrowing headroom versus the regulatory 50% limit and increasing sensitivity to asset devaluations and refinancing costs; total debt (incl. perpetual securities) to NAV is 85.9%.

~70% of revenue is non-SGD (JPY, HKD, RMB, KRW, AUD, MYR, VND, INR); FY25/26 saw a S$325.0m currency translation loss on portfolio valuation and ongoing SGD strength versus regional currencies continues to pressure revenue/NPI/DPU; only ~75% of income is hedged into SGD.

17% of debt remains unhedged/floating; ICR sensitivity shows a 100bps rate rise would cut ICR from 2.9x to 2.2x; S$89m of debt matures in FY26/27 requiring refinancing, albeit backed by S$716m of committed facilities.

Management ceased distributing one-off divestment gains from FY25/26, structurally lowering headline DPU (down 9.8% y-o-y) versus prior years that included such gains, even though underlying/adjusted DPU fell a smaller 3.4%.

regulatory.description: Singapore's Code on Collective Investment Schemes caps aggregate leverage (currently 50% with ICR-based conditions) and governs related-party transaction disclosure; MLT operates within but is trending toward these limits.
Operating across nine countries exposes MLT to varying foreign ownership, tax, land-lease and repatriation rules, particularly in China, Vietnam and India.

macro.description: Management cites the evolving Middle East conflict, elevated energy prices, and IMF's lowered global growth forecast (3.1%, down from 3.3%) as risks to leasing demand and borrowing costs, though direct electricity cost exposure is low (<2% of property expenses).

China GDP growth target lowered to 4.5-5.0% for 2026 (lowest since 1991) signalling a structural shift from scale-driven to quality-driven growth, with continued soft domestic consumption weighing on logistics rents.

REIT valuations and NAV are sensitive to cap rate movements; portfolio valuation fell 1.6% y-o-y in FY25/26, with NAV per unit down 3.8% to S$1.26, partly cushioned by fair value gains ex-China/Hong Kong.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Asia-Pacific logistics real estate remains supported by long-term e-commerce growth and supply-chain diversification, but near-term conditions are mixed: developed markets (Singapore, Japan, Australia, South Korea) show positive rental reversions and tight supply, while China and (to a lesser extent) Hong Kong face oversupply, soft consumption and falling rents.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - logistics/industrial real estate is less cyclical than retail/office but tied to consumer spending, trade volumes and e-commerce penetration; REIT structure amplifies sensitivity to interest rates and cap rates
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - as a leveraged, income-distributing REIT, unit price and distributable income are sensitive to SGD and regional base rates; 17% of debt unhedged and loans/hedges roll off at higher rates over time
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High - ~70% of revenue generated outside Singapore in JPY, HKD, RMB, KRW, AUD, MYR, VND and INR; partially hedged (75% of 12-month income, 83% of debt into fixed rates) but FX translation materially affects reported NAV and DPU

recent_developments.event: FY25/26 full-year results: gross revenue S$708.3m (-2.6% y-o-y), NPI S$610.2m (-2.4%), DPU 7.262 cents (-9.8% y-o-y, or -3.4% excluding divestment gains); 4Q DPU 1.819 cents marked the fourth consecutive quarter of steady operational DPU
Completed accretive acquisition of a freehold, 100%-leased Grade A warehouse in Bhiwandi, Mumbai, India for ~S$53.2m, extending MLT's India network beyond Pune and Delhi
Divested six non-core properties (Singapore x3, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia) for ~S$99m combined at ~20% average premium to book valuation, as part of portfolio rejuvenation
Completed S$205m redevelopment of Mapletree Joo Koon Logistics Hub in Singapore; now fully leased with building occupancy at 99.3%

Management formally discontinued distributing one-off divestment gains to unitholders as a prudent capital-management measure amid macro uncertainty, redirecting retained gains to debt paydown and AEIs
China rental reversions continued improving (-2.0% in 4Q FY25/26 vs -9.4% a year earlier) though still negative, while all other markets posted positive reversions (portfolio ex-China +4.2%)

Board renewal: Mr Lim Joo Boon retired as Independent Director/AC Chairman after reaching the 9-year independence tenure limit; Ms Ong Siew Koon (ex-EY audit/finance) and Mr Lee Wai Fai (ex-UOB banking veteran) appointed as new Independent Non-Executive Directors
MLT co-won the Most Transparent Company Award (REITs & Business Trusts category) at the SIAS Investors' Choice Awards 2025

Analyst commentary: JPMorgan maintained Overweight but cut price target to S$1.40 (May 2026), calling distributions stabilised; CGS International, DBS and Morningstar cut targets to S$1.40-S$1.63 earlier in 2026 after the FY24/25 DPU decline of ~10.6%; Citi maintained a S$1.56 target; consensus target around S$1.39-S$1.55 with the stock trading well below most targets, implying analysts view it as undervalued despite the DPU decline

items.target: Discontinue distribution of one-off divestment gains; retained gains redirected to debt paydown or AEI funding
items.notes: Structural policy shift lowers headline DPU trajectory vs FY23/24-FY24/25 periods that included divestment-gain distributions of S$41.6m and S$27.0m respectively

items.target: Refinance ~S$89m of FY26/27 debt maturities using S$716m of committed undrawn credit facilities; maintain hedging at ~83% of debt fixed and ~75% of income hedged into SGD
items.notes: No specific leverage ceiling given, but management states a focus on preserving financial flexibility and prudent capital management

items.target: Continue selective divestments (targeting up to ~S$1bn of older-specification assets, ~half in China/Hong Kong) and redeploy proceeds into accretive acquisitions and AEIs
items.notes: No specific $ acquisition/divestment target for FY26/27 was quantified; described qualitatively as 'actively pursuing accretive acquisitions, asset enhancements and selective divestments'

items.target: Prioritise healthy occupancy, rental stability and cost efficiency
items.notes: No specific numeric occupancy target disclosed; portfolio occupancy was 96.9% as at 31 March 2026

items.target: Expand self-funded solar generating capacity to 100 MWp by 2030
items.notes: FY25/26 self-funded capacity reached 58.9 MWp (+24% y-o-y); total (incl. third-party funded) reached 131.8 MWp

items.target: Achieve green certification for >80% of portfolio GFA by 2030
items.notes: FY25/26 reached 66-67% of portfolio GFA, already exceeding the FY25/26 interim target of 60%

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jean Kam described FY25/26 as 'resilient' despite a 'challenging operating environment marked by macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties,' citing stable same-store performance and the completed Joo Koon redevelopment as offsets to divestment and currency headwinds. Chairman Lee Chong Kwee flagged continued SGD strength against regional currencies and rising borrowing costs on refinanced debt as the main near-term pressures on distributions, while noting leasing activity and tenant behavior have remained stable. Management is 'closely monitoring' second-order effects from the evolving Middle East conflict on economic sentiment and leasing demand, but direct exposure to oil/energy costs is limited (<2% of property expenses).

bull_case: Highly diversified, well-occupied (96.9%) portfolio across nine Asia-Pacific markets with investment-grade (Fitch BBB+) credit and disciplined, multi-currency hedging limiting downside from any single market or currency

Sponsor (Mapletree Investments) provides a visible, de-risked acquisition pipeline via ROFR, including development projects underway in India, Vietnam, Malaysia and Australia that can be injected once stabilised and accretive

Four consecutive quarters of stable-to-rising operational DPU (ex-divestment gains), positive rental reversions in every market except China (+4.2% ex-China in 4Q FY25/26), and an improving China reversion trend (-2.0% vs -9.4% a year ago) suggest the operating trough may be behind it

Portfolio rejuvenation strategy (divesting older China/Hong Kong assets at ~20% premiums to redeploy into modern, higher-growth logistics space) should improve the quality and growth profile of the portfolio over time

Trading well below analyst consensus price targets (S$1.39-S$1.63 vs. recent unit price around S$1.15), several brokers (JPMorgan, Citi, CGS International, DBS) view the stock as undervalued with an attractive ~6% distribution yield
Structural e-commerce and supply-chain diversification tailwinds support long-term logistics real estate demand
bear_case: DPU has declined for multiple consecutive years (8.787 cents FY21/22 to 7.262 cents FY25/26), and the newly adopted policy of withholding divestment-gain distributions removes a lever that previously supported headline payouts

Persistent structural weakness in China (18.3% of AUM) and soft Hong Kong SAR (22.3% of AUM) leasing markets, with elevated vacancy and continued negative rental reversions in China, represent a large, slow-to-recover portion of the portfolio

Rising aggregate leverage (40.6%, up from 36.8% three years ago) combined with ~17% of debt still unhedged leaves distributable income exposed to further rate increases and reduces balance-sheet flexibility
Heavy non-SGD revenue exposure (~70%) amid a strong Singapore Dollar continues to produce currency translation losses on both NAV (S$325.0m loss in FY25/26) and distributable income despite hedging

External sponsor-managed REIT structure creates inherent conflicts of interest around ROFR-sourced acquisition pricing, management fees, and timing of asset transactions between MLT and the broader Mapletree group

Global macro uncertainty (Middle East conflict, elevated energy prices, slowing IMF global growth forecast of 3.1%) could further dampen leasing demand and keep borrowing costs elevated longer than expected
